payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing

decision.question: Compared with the source, has the image been perceptibly transformed toward a pencil drawing, and is that transformation pervasive enough to render the scene as a whole in pencil-drawn style?
decision.criteria: Pass only if the scene as a whole is clearly and pervasively rendered as a pencil drawing, with visible pencil-like linework and shading representing the scene. Fail if there is no perceptible change toward pencil drawing, or if the change is limited to muted color, grain, or other effects without visible pencil-like marks or shading. If there is perceptible pencil-like treatment but it is incomplete or the scene remains substantially photographic, mark this condition as unknown rather than fail. Unknown also applies when visual evidence is genuinely insufficient to determine whether there is perceptible progress or pervasive completion.
decision.binding: Compare the supplied source image with the edited image. Assess visible evidence of actual pencil-like marks and shading across the scene: distinguish no perceptible pencil-drawing progress from incomplete but perceptible stylization, and require pervasive whole-scene pencil rendering for pass. Muted color or grain alone is not sufficient evidence of progress.
